nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of NiMoO4·H2O
nodes.procedure: Firstly, a piece of nickel foam (2×3 cm²) was immersed in the solution containing 0.04 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 0.01 M (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O with 15 ml H2O and transferred into a 25 mL Teflon vessel. Then, the vessel was sealed in a stainless autoclave and heated to 150°C and kept for 6 h. After cooling down to room temperature, the NiMoO4·H2O washed with DI water and ethanol and dried in an oven at 60°C.

nodes.name: Nitridation to NiMoN
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared NiMoO4·H2O nanorods were heated to 500°C at a ramp rate of 5°C/min and maintained for 2 h in NH3 atmosphere. After the furnace naturally cooled down to room temperature and NiMoN nanorods were obtained.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of NiFe LDH on NiMoN
nodes.procedure: The NiFe LDH nanosheets were electrodeposited on the surface of NiMoN nanorods to obtain NiMoN/NiFe LDH. The electrodeposition was conducted in a standard three-electrode setup, using NiMoN as working electrode, a parallel platinum net as counter electrode and Ag/AgCl(saturated) as reference electrode. The electrolyte was containing 0.06 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 0.048 M Fe(NO3)3·9H2O. The electrodeposition potential was -1.0 V vs. Ag/AgCl for 200 s. Then, the as-synthesized electrode was rinsed with deionized water and ethanol and dried at 60°C. The loading weight of the formed electrocatalysts on the nickel foam was ≈15.8 mg cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show diffraction peaks at 36.5° and 65.7° indexed to (100) and (110) planes of Ni0.2Mo0.8N; NiMoN/NiFe LDH shows no obvious diffraction peaks except for Ni0.2Mo0.8N, indicating amorphous and ultrathin NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of NiMoN/NiFe LDH are shown in Fig. 1b. ... After the electrodeposition process of NiFe LDH nanosheets on NiMoN nanorods (Fig. 1b), no obvious diffraction peak can be detected except for two diffraction peaks from Ni0.2Mo0.8N, indicating the amorphous and ultrathin feature of NiFe LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows ultrathin NiFe LDH nanosheets vertically and densely distributed on NiMoN nanorods surface, forming 3D hierarchical architecture.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1c, d, the ultrathin NiFe LDH nanosheets were vertically and densely distributed on the surface of NiMoN nanorods, indicating the formation of 3D hierarchical architecture of NiMoN/NiFe LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms NiMoN nanorods cores with NiFe LDH nanosheets shells; HR-TEM shows heterointerface with lattice fringe d-spacing of 0.28 nm attributed to (001) plane of NiMoN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The detailed heterostructure of NiMoN/NiFe LDH was further confirmed by TEM images (Fig. 1e, f). ... The lattice fringe with a d-spacing of 0.28 nm is attributed to the (001) plane of NiMoN, whereas the shell is dominated by the amorphous NiFe LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDX mapping show Ni, Mo, N, Fe and O elements homogeneously distributed throughout NiMoN/NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) and energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) mapping images showed that Ni, Mo, N, Fe and O elements are distributed in the entire region.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p binding energies: NiMoN shows 852.8, 855.8, 870.1, 873.6 eV (Ni-N, Ni2+); NiMoN/NiFe LDH shows positive shift to 856.2, 873.9 eV indicating charge transfer. Mo 3d: NiMoN shows Mo3+, Mo4+, Mo6+; NiMoN/NiFe LDH shows Mo4+, Mo6+. Fe 2p: 710.9, 712.5, 724.5, 726.3 eV (Fe2+, Fe3+) with negative shift. N 1s: 395.6, 398.3, 399.9 eV (Mo 3p, Ni/Mo-N, N-H).
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the Ni 2p spectra in Fig. 2a, the binding energy of 852.8, 855.8, 870.1 and 873.6 eV are ascribed to Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2 of Ni-N and Ni2+ for NiMoN nanorods, respectively... The Fe 2p XPS spectra of NiMoN/NiFe LDH in Fig. 2c shows four deconvoluted peaks at 710.9, 712.5, 724.5 and 726.3 eV, corresponding to Fe 2p3/2 and Fe 2p1/2 of Fe2+ and Fe3+, respectively... The N 1s spectra of NiMoN shows three peaks at 395.6, 398.3 and 399.9 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl values from CV: as-activated NiMoN/NiFe LDH = 11.4 mF cm^-2, NiFe LDH = 7.5 mF cm^-2, NiMoN = 4.1 mF cm^-2, indicating more exposed active sites from hierarchical architecture.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ECSA value was measured through the electrochemical double-layer capacitances (Cdl) determined by cyclic voltammetry method. As-activated NiMoN/NiFe LDH possesses the highest Cdl value of 11.4 mF cm^-2, which is higher than those of NiFe LDH (7.5 mF cm^-2) and NiMoN (4.1 mF cm^-2).

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman shows Ni-O at 532 cm^-1, Fe-O at 702 cm^-1, Mo-O at 890 cm^-1 at OCP; beyond 1.35 V, peaks at 473 and 551 cm^-1 indicate γ-NiOOH formation and O-O vibration at 900-1100 cm^-1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At the open circuit potential (OCP), NiMoN/NiFe LDH and NiFe LDH show characteristic peaks at 532 and 702 cm^-1, which can be attributed to Ni-O in disordered Ni(OH)2 and Fe-O in γ-FeOOH, respectively. ... two characteristic peaks appeared at 473 and 551 cm^-1 beyond 1.35 V, corresponding to Eg bending and A1g stretching vibration of NiIII-O in γ-NiOOH.
